% [MAIN 2]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{The metric battery.} Ten measurements of the same edge. Metric~1 defines the candidate set and 2--7 grade it. Metric~2a is named honestly as a \emph{contribution filter} rather than as Tree SAE's $S_\mathrm{res}$: two strong but unrelated co-firing features pass both of its legs, and its pass rate scales with block energy. The probe-based $S_\mathrm{res}$ is 2b, and its target is the self-label $\mathbf{1}[f_c > 0]$, so a corrupted latent yields a probe that validates its own corruption; we report it as self-labeled and as a self-consistency check, not as ground truth.}
  \label{tab:battery}
  \begin{tabular}{llllr}
    \toprule
     & Metric & What it asks & Threshold & Module \\
    \midrule
    1a & Reverse coverage $R$ & $P(\text{parent} \mid \text{child})$ & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{coverage} \\
    1b & Forward coverage $F$ & $P(\text{child} \mid \text{parent})$ & reported & \texttt{coverage} \\
    1c & Joint-child coverage & $R_\mathrm{supp}$, $R_\mathrm{mass}$, energy share & reported & \texttt{joint\_child} \\
    2a & Reconstruction ablation & both features carry mass on the child's tokens & $\geq 0.01$ & \texttt{reconstruction} \\
    2b & Probe $S_\mathrm{res}$ & both decoders near the child-concept probe & top-5 rank & \texttt{sres} \\
    3 & Sibling redundancy & co-activation among one parent's children & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{sibling\_redundancy} \\
    4 & Out-degree & one parent covering most of the next block & $\geq 30\%$ & \texttt{outdegree} \\
    5 & Token-frequency control & does the edge survive on rare tokens & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{token\_control} \\
    6 & Independence null & PMI against independent firing & $> 0$ & \texttt{independence\_null} \\
    7 & In-block directed coverage & containment within one block, and duplicates & asymmetry & \texttt{in\_block\_edges} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

  \caption{\textbf{What each metric can separate.} A candidate pair can look like an edge for seven reasons and only one is hierarchy, so the question per metric is which column it adds, not whether it is correct. $\bullet$ detects, $\circ$ partial (necessary but not sufficient, or only in some regimes), -- blind. \textbf{These cells are read off each metric's construction and are not a measured accuracy}; every one is exercised by a row of Table~\ref{tab:tier1}. % [MAIN 4]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{Four tiers, trading ground truth against realism.} Each rung licenses the one above it: Tier~1 proves the arithmetic and nothing about whether an SAE would learn such a structure. Tier~2 attacks that gap, but on Bussmann's 20-feature tree with 9 edges and no injected pathologies rather than on the pathology-injected world Tier~1 grades, so it changes the world as well as the statistics and does not isolate training as the single moving part either. What it does isolate cleanly is blame: only what the SAE actually learned reaches the metrics, so a missed edge counts against a metric only if the SAE learned both endpoints. Tier~3 inserts a base model between the concepts and the SAE, which Tiers~1 and~2 do not have at all. It is \textbf{not} a controlled swap from Tier~2: the grammar, the base model, the corpus and the dictionary size all change together, so it \emph{bounds} the base model's contribution rather than isolating it --- isolating it would mean training a transformer on Bussmann's own tree. Its grammar is known but nothing yet maps a latent to a grammar symbol, so its result column reports the same battery outputs as Tier~4 rather than a recovery score; the helper that would close the gap (\texttt{role\_of} in the PCFG repo) already exists. Tier~4 is named \emph{released} rather than \emph{real} --- Tier~3 is a real SAE too, really trained over a really trained transformer, and the distinction that matters is that Tier~4 is a published checkpoint we did not train. That is also a constraint and not only a label: we do not control its dictionary, which is why the $S_\mathrm{res}$ column of Table~\ref{tab:gemma} exists for one layer only. It has no known answer at all.}
  \label{tab:tiers}
  \begin{tabular}{llll}
    \toprule
    Tier & Runs on & Ground truth & Result \\
    \midrule
    1 Synthetic toy & \parbox[t]{0.22\linewidth}{\raggedright hand-built statistics\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.18\linewidth}{\raggedright by construction\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.25\linewidth}{\raggedright 14/14 rows, 21/21 functions\strut} \\
    2 Trained toy & \parbox[t]{0.22\linewidth}{\raggedright an SAE trained on Bussmann's tree\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.18\linewidth}{\raggedright Bussmann's tree is known\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.25\linewidth}{\raggedright precision 1.00, recall 0.67\strut} \\
    3 PCFG SAE & \parbox[t]{0.22\linewidth}{\raggedright a Matryoshka SAE over a 4-layer transformer trained on a PCFG corpus\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.18\linewidth}{\raggedright the grammar is known; no latent$\leftrightarrow$symbol mapping yet\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.25\linewidth}{\raggedright 2 layers, 327--781 candidates; \emph{no ground-truth score} --- same battery outputs as Tier~4\strut} \\
    4 Released SAE & \parbox[t]{0.22\linewidth}{\raggedright \texttt{google/gemma-2-2b}\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.18\linewidth}{\raggedright none --- human reading\strut} & \parbox[t]{0.25\linewidth}{\raggedright 48 survivors read against autointerp labels\strut} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \\[2pt] \footnotesize Tier~4's dictionary is the released \texttt{gemma-2-2b-res-matryoshka-dc}. Tier~3, per layer: layer~01: 327 candidates, 100\% recon, 0/327 $S_\mathrm{res}$; layer~03: 781 candidates, 95\% recon, 4/772 $S_\mathrm{res}$. Lateral control (not a tier): 6/6 testable true edges run early block $\rightarrow$ late on the trained toy.
\end{table}

% [APP 3]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{What the cross-source comparison rests on, and how far to trust it.} Two questions, both of which are usually settled silently. \emph{First}, comparing base models of different depth needs a rule for pairing their layers, and the two defensible rules pick opposite ends of gemma: by block index PCFG's layers pair with gemma's L1 and L3, by relative depth $(L{+}1)/N$ with gemma's L12 and L24. Block index wins on the mean (8.8 points against 13.8), which is why it is what Figure~\ref{fig:cross-source-layer-response} draws---though the margin rests largely on one measure, and the reconstruction filter is inert on PCFG in any case. \emph{Second}, a small gap is only impressive if the measure could have been far apart. The last two columns ask that: \emph{range} is how far each measure moves across all 8 graded runs, and the ratio is the gap against it. The two readings do not agree---edges improving reconstruction is near the bottom on raw points and near the top on the ratio---so both are printed and neither is called correct. The honest summary is that the three measures with the smallest raw gaps are also the three pinned against a boundary ($\geq 2$ parents at 89--100\%, sibling redundancy at 3--6\%, the frequency control at 0--2\%), where agreement costs the two sources nothing. \textbf{On 2 shared layers none of this is a result.}}
  \label{tab:align}
  \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}

    \midrule

    children with $\geq$ 2 parents & 0.6 & 0.6 & 11.2 & 0.05 \\
    sibling redundancy (mean Jaccard) & 1.0 & 0.4 & 3.0 & 0.33 \\
    fan-out concentration (Gini) & 5.8 & 5.9 & 7.9 & 0.73 \\
    edges improving reconstruction & 9.6 & 33.8 & 46.1 & 0.21 \\
    edges at chance for the base rate & 35.4 & 40.4 & 77.0 & 0.46 \\
    \textbf{mean} & \textbf{8.8} & \textbf{13.8} &  &  \\
    \bottomrule

\end{table}

% [APP 4]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{The rank rule's null depends on dictionary size.} $S_\mathrm{res}$ passes an edge when both decoders fall in the top $k = 5$ of the probe's correlations over the whole dictionary. It is a geometry test, so an unrelated parent passes whenever chance puts it there, at a rate of $k/D$. The same $k$ is therefore two orders of magnitude stricter on gemma than on a 42-feature toy, and a measured pass rate is only interpretable against its own null: two runs on the \emph{same} 1{,}792-latent dictionary land on opposite sides of theirs. Reporting $S_\mathrm{res}$ shares across sources without this correction compares nothing.}
  \label{tab:null}
  \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
    \toprule
    Source & $D$ & Null $k/D$ & Observed & vs.\ null \\
    \midrule
    Synthetic toy (Tier 1) & 42 & 11.9\% & --- & --- \\
    Trained toy (Tier 2) & 20 & 25.0\% & 5/5 true edges & --- \\
    \texttt{gemma-2-2b} L6 & 32,768 & 0.015\% & 0.59\% & 39$\times$ \\
    PCFG layer 01 & 1,792 & 0.279\% & 0.00\% & below chance \\
    PCFG layer 03 & 1,792 & 0.279\% & 0.52\% & 2$\times$ \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
